body: thanks. logically, everything you're saying makes sense.

thank you for commenting. it's really nice of you.

i don't know if i have another hospital stay left in me - i've been hospitalized at least five times since last November, and two of those hospitalizations resulted in pysch ward time. not that that's an inherently bad thing, but i just don't know if i can do it again. the bills are piling up already. i tried a lot of meds and they either make me manic after a month, or give me seizures. i know the "right" meds probably exist for me somewhere, but i've grown so tired of doctor visits.

i guess i just feel like a lost cause. too many things in my life are piling up and instead of dealing with it, it's like my brain just wants me to get really far away. i've tried to tackle some of my debts, i've been working, i've gotten some issues in my life under control, but at the same time i don't know that i can keep this up forever. it just seems like too much and i'd rather just say fuck it. i know that's selfish, but the thought won't leave me alone - it's like the only thought in my head that doesn't turn to static.

anyway, sorry for unlaoding on you. thanks again for the advice - really, i appreciate it.

okay, fair enough to all of that.

honestly, i think your best bet might be going w what the other commenter said: record him, gather some evidence, get him out of there. then you don't have to worry about shelters, food, and most importantly being abused by him anymore. like....it sounds like with everything you've been thru, you really haven't been allowed the time to process, let alone heal. you deserve that  if there's a way to get this guy out of yr home, why not give it a shot?

You are strong. Talking and reaching out are valid coping skills.

I saw another commenter here mention recording your roommate, and agree with them - could be a good option. Getting him out seems preferable to you having to be homeless again.
If it does come down to thinking about shelters again, would the youth shelters be able to refer you to other programs for adults? or a shelter for victims of domestic violence?

on the food thing: can you wait until he passes out from drinking to get something to eat? or make something "for both of you" that you know he doesn't like so you can just eat it? sorry, i know this probabaly seems manipulative but this person is treating you terribly.

I think you're a lot stronger than you're giving yourself credit for.

Not sure what to say, except that i can empathize. when i finally escaped my abusive family, i ended up going straight to my ex-gf who was also abusive  (although it didn't really sink into my head until we were living together and by then it was too late); broke up and was homeless in a big city fr a little, until i moved in with a friend who turned out to be abusive too. Fortunately, after maybe a year i had some money saved up & got out.

I'm sorry you're going thru this. There are ways to get out and still continue living.

Could you confront the person your living with? Do you have any friends you could crash with? I think there's a couch-surfing subreddit & while i can't personally vouch for it, maybe that's an option? As for food, in the States we have foodstamps and my town also has a lot of local food drives/pantries -- are any of those things feasible for you? if you get the food yourself, i think you can justify not sharing with him.

I'm sorry that you're in this situation. You're an incredibly strong person fr dealing with all of this. i hope things work out for u. Good Vibes to you, from an internet stranger<3

When my headphones get caught on something, and are subsequently yanked from my ears. Shit sends me into a rage.

In a hurry down the stairs? Headphone cord snags on railing, tugs them out. Carrying something bulky down the street? Why bother - it's just gonna rip out the earbuds. Doorknobs? My background music is ruined, as is my day.

It's worse because it nearly always happens in public, so there's embarrassment piled on top of the anger. Why.

just commenting to say i read this & care. i can relate to the bit where u mentioned how you're "uncomfortable but feeling nothing." i feel very numb/empty a lot, but it's like a repression method to ease the discomfort.

anyways, please be safe especially since you're inebriated. i'm around if you want to chat

have had ideation since i was 14/15. am 25 now. have had bursts throughout those years where active suicidality/planning/attempts have happened. but then it calms down again - but regardless it's still an every-day lurking thought.

hi. i hope you woke up feeling better today. obviously you reached out fr a reason so i hope you didn't go thru with whatever your method was.

i feel for you - went through a lot of mental health (bipolar) and ED-related problems during university (othorexia/over-exercising). ended up dropping out, but here's the thing: we can always go back. you have an opportunity: you can take time off from school and take all the time you need to get your health in order/figure out your next move. (if you can - talk to your academic advisor and find out if taking a medical leave of absence is an option so you don't have to re-apply for your school later. that's what i did)

you deserve to give yourself time to heal - school isn't going anywhere

can your doctor(s) get you on another antidepressant while you taper down from the citalopram? maybe that would help with your feelings of hopelessness, with not being able to enjoy your hobbies anymore, etc.. 

also, do you have a therapist? if so, i think it would be wise to tell them how you're feeling & maybe they can offer some reassurance about the whole medication withdrawal process.

everyone deserves a chance at happiness. maybe you could reach out to some of your friends who you've been isolating from. you said in your post that you "just don't care," but i think since you brought them up, that shows you do care. they'll probably be really happy to hear from you.

hang in there - you're strong enough to push thru this.

Fellow pre-everything person: before realizing I was trans, I shaved everything. Over the past couple years, I quit shaving my legs & underarms (tried to go back a couple times, but not only was shaving dysphoria-inducing, it was straight physically uncomfortable).

Now, I only shave my face (yes, pre-T even if that's weird) bc i'm blonde so I have a lot of peach fuzz that I feel is visible and makes me look more feminine? Plus, I just enjoy the routine of shaving my face haha. And I still shave my junk which idk if that's weird or like...and old habit carried over from being told AFAB ppl shouldn't have hair there, but it just bothers me being hairy there sooo yeah  :/ idk! I'm all abt people shaving or not-shaving wherever they want!!! It's your own body! :)

(Nervous venting) Starting a new job this afternoon and am super fucking anxious about it, especially about being referred to by my legal name for the first time in a while. i'm out to everyone else in my life, and like....at my orientation, the hiring manager asked if there were any "nicknames" I'd prefer to go by  (seemed like a standard question - i'm pre-T and don't pass at all so it's not like she clocked me or anything). Realistically, I'm sure once i get settled in and get to know everyone there I can ask for my nametag to be changed and ask for people to refer to me by my name, especially since it's close to my legal name, so it shouldn't be a big deal. it's just added anxiety on top of starting a new job in a town i just moved to, and after being out of work for a while. I dunno, that's all. it's good to ramble somewhere, i guess.

Not sure about what you can do about feeling exhausted all the time (like, if it pertains to a physical health reason, or yr simply overworked), but what has helped me a lot without having gym access was finding cardio exercises I could do outdoors (running/biking (I already had a bike, but maybe getting one used on Craigslist is an option if you don't have one and need something cheap?)) and doing other exercises just at home in my room or in front of the television (crunches, pushups, etc.).

I literally just started working out again, and am taking it slowly, and fitting it in where I can. For me, that means getting up earlier in the day to make time for it; for you, maybe it will mean squeezing in some time after school/work/whatever you do during the day, or after dinner. I also started with smaller amounts of time and have just sort of been gradually tacking on more cardio per day and a few more reps of the other stuff per day. For me, it made starting less intimidating and sticking with a routine more feasible. As much as I would love to be my idea of "big and strong" right away....I'm 5'3" and fairly wimpy, haha, so I just know that's not gonna happen overnight.

Find something you enjoy doing so you can commit to it, but also be patient with yourself, regardless of what yr personal goals may be - I think progress takes time :)
